item.title: WNBA season set to begin May 8 if new CBA is reached, league will take 17-day FIBA World Cup break
item.description: The WNBA is set to begin its season on May 8, assuming the league and the players’ union can come to an agreement on a new collective bargaining agreement. item.title: Trump cancels tariff threat over Greenland, says NATO agreed to ‘framework’ of future Arctic deal
item.description: President Donald Trump announced Wednesday that he was scrapping his planned tariffs on eight European nations in an effort to force U.S. control over Greenland, pulling a dramatic reversal shortly after insisting he wanted to get the island “including right, title and ownership.” The post Trump cancels tariff threat over Greenland, says NATO agreed to ‘framework’ of future Arctic deal appeared first on The Dispatch.

item.title: Supreme Court seems inclined to keep Lisa Cook on Fed board despite Trump attempt to fire her
item.description: The Supreme Court on Wednesday seemed inclined to keep Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook in her job, casting doubt on President Donald Trump’s bid to wrest control of the nation’s central bank. item.title: Trump’s Board of Peace is dividing countries in Europe and the Middle East
item.description: Divisions emerged Wednesday over U.S. President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace as its ambitions have grown beyond Gaza, with some Western European countries declining to join, others remaining noncommittal and a group of Muslim countries agreeing to sign on. item.title: Immigration officers assert sweeping power to enter homes without a judge’s warrant, memo says
item.description: Federal immigration officers are asserting sweeping power to forcibly enter people’s homes without a judge’s warrant, according to an internal Immigration and Customs Enforcement memo obtained by The Associated Press, marking a sharp reversal of longstanding guidance meant to respect constitutional limits on government searches. The post Immigration officers assert sweeping power to enter homes without a judge’s warrant, memo says appeared first on The Dispatch.

item.title: Iconic Coney Island hot dog hawker Nathan’s Famous is sold for $450 million
item.description: Nathan’s Famous, which opened as a 5-cent hot dog stand in Coney Island more than a century ago, has been sold to packaged meat giant Smithfield Foods in an all-cash $450 million deal, the companies announced Wednesday.
